newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq solves problem, oil ready to flow - official.
newsitem.headline: Iraq solves problem, oil ready to flow - official.

text.p: A small technical problem held up the flow of Iraqi crude to Turkey for a short time but Iraqi technicians solved it very quickly, an official said on Wednesday.
"There was a small fault. We have overcome that very quickly. Oil is now ready to flow any time," Taha Hmud Mosa, senior undersecretary of Iraq's oil ministry, told Reuters.
Mosa said Iraq did not need to pump oil right now as storage facilities at the Turkish terminal of Ceyhan were full and the twin pipeline was also full.
He said Iraq had cleared a deal with Turkish refiners Tupras for the loading of 75,000 barrels per day of oil and the Turkish company would lift the crude within 24 hours.

He said Iraq would then immediately start pumping to replace the crude lifted by Tupras. "Within the coming hours, we shall complete the usual arrangements to nominate the tanker and start pumping simultaneously," he said.
"There is no problem at the moment," said Mosa. "Part of the problem raised earlier was because we did not have ready deals."

An official from the state organisation for the marketing of oil SOMO said more and more foreign companies were lining up in Baghdad for oil deals. "Yes, they are coming in droves. Some of them are here. Some of them are on their way from Amman to Baghdad. Some others are on their way from their countries to Amman," he said.
He reiterated that demand for Iraqi oil was higher than the limit of about 650,000 barrels a day set by the U.N.
